title: Colossal Chestnut Chocolate Cake
tagline: Dense, dark and faintly ridiculous, with a pink cloud on top.

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, plus a little extra for the tin

steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan. Grease a 20cm round tin with a little butter and line the base with baking paper. Defrost the raspberries now.
Melt the chocolate and 150g butter in a heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water. Stir until glossy, then take off the heat to cool slightly.
Beat the chestnut purée with 130g sugar until smooth. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the cooled chocolate, cocoa and salt until just combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until set at the edges with a slight wobble in the middle. Cool in the tin for 20 minutes.
Whip the cream with the remaining 20g sugar to soft peaks. Lightly crush the raspberries with a fork, then fold through for pink ripples.
Turn the cake out, peel off the paper and pile on the raspberry cream. Slice with a hot knife. Serve slightly warm.
image_prompt: A tall round dark chocolate chestnut cake, dense and fudgy with a cracked glossy top, crowned with a generous swirl of raspberry-ripple pink whipped cream and a few crushed raspberries. One thick slice cut out showing the moist, almost black crumb, on a plain white plate.
alt_text: A dark, fudgy chocolate cake topped with pink raspberry-rippled cream, with one thick slice cut to show the dense crumb.
caption_hook: A cake so chocolatey it should come with its own weather warning. Roald Dahl would have asked for a second slice. Who's brave enough to go back for thirds?
